blocks.rationale: Create a narrowly scoped helper for section 152(b)(1). The current rule turns on whether the individual is a dependent of a taxpayer; a qualifying child is a dependent, so the helper can evaluate the positive applicability claim from one current-facts boolean without encoding names or case answers.

inputs.name: individual_is_dependent_of_a_taxpayer
inputs.question: Do the current facts establish that the individual addressed by the proposition is a dependent of a taxpayer for the relevant taxable year, including by being that taxpayer's qualifying child or qualifying relative?

skill.intent: Determine whether a positive claim that section 152(b)(1) applies to the current individual is supported because the individual is a dependent of a taxpayer for the relevant year.

outputs.description: The native label Entailment when section 152(b)(1) applies to the individual, otherwise Contradiction.
outputs.name: answer

fields.name: individual_is_dependent_of_a_taxpayer
fields.question: Is the current individual a dependent of a taxpayer for the relevant taxable year?

reads.question: Read the current facts and applicable dependent definitions to determine whether the individual addressed by the proposition is a dependent of a taxpayer for the relevant year.
reads.source_locator: current source native view source_text, referenced sections, facts, and question

origin.quote:
For purposes of this subtitle, the term "dependent" means-

    (1) a qualifying child, or

    (2) a qualifying relative.

source_obligations.statement: Determine whether the individual is a dependent of a taxpayer, including because the individual is a qualifying child under subsection (a).

origin.quote: If an individual is a dependent of a taxpayer for any taxable year of such taxpayer beginning in a calendar year, such individual shall be treated as having no dependents for any taxable year of such individual beginning in such calendar year.

source_obligations.statement: If the current individual is a dependent of a taxpayer, apply the rule that the individual is treated as having no dependents for the corresponding calendar year.

source_provenance.quote:
For purposes of this subtitle, the term "dependent" means-

    (1) a qualifying child, or

    (2) a qualifying relative.

If an individual is a dependent of a taxpayer for any taxable year of such taxpayer beginning in a calendar year, such individual shall be treated as having no dependents for any taxable year of such individual beginning in such calendar year.

blocks.rationale: Create a section 63(c)(5) applicability helper that asks only whether the statutory prerequisite is established for the current individual. This directly addresses the trigger failure while avoiding the unrelated progressive-tax schedule reader.

inputs.name: section_151_deduction_allowable_to_another_taxpayer
inputs.question: Do the current facts establish that a deduction under section 151 for the individual addressed by the proposition is allowable to another taxpayer for a taxable year beginning in the same calendar year?

skill.intent: Determine whether a positive claim that section 63(c)(5) applies to the current individual's basic standard deduction is supported by a section 151 deduction being allowable to another taxpayer.

outputs.description: The native label Entailment when section 63(c)(5) applies, otherwise Contradiction.
outputs.name: answer

fields.name: section_151_deduction_allowable_to_another_taxpayer
fields.question: Is a section 151 deduction for the current individual allowable to another taxpayer for the relevant calendar year?

reads.question: Read the current facts and proposition to determine whether another taxpayer is entitled to a section 151 deduction for the individual whose basic standard deduction is at issue.
reads.source_locator: current source native view source_text, referenced section 151, facts, and question

origin.quote: In the case of an individual with respect to whom a deduction under section 151 is allowable to another taxpayer for a taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the individual's taxable year begins

source_obligations.statement: Check whether the current record establishes that a section 151 deduction for the individual is allowable to another taxpayer in the corresponding calendar year.

origin.quote:
the basic standard deduction applicable to such individual for such individual's taxable year shall not exceed the greater of-

        (A) $500, or

        (B) the sum of $250 and such individual's earned income.

source_obligations.statement: Apply section 63(c)(5) only when its prerequisite that the section 151 deduction is allowable to another taxpayer is satisfied.

source_provenance.quote:
In the case of an individual with respect to whom a deduction under section 151 is allowable to another taxpayer for a taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the individual's taxable year begins, the basic standard deduction applicable to such individual for such individual's taxable year shall not exceed the greater of-

        (A) $500, or

        (B) the sum of $250 and such individual's earned income.

blocks.rationale: Create a compact airline terminal helper around one coupled current-source assessment of final per-item fees. Keeping the fees aligned by item preserves checked-bag ordinal effects and lets the deterministic program perform only the final summation.

inputs.name: ticket_price
inputs.question: What integer ticket price is stated for the current passenger?

inputs.name: per_item_final_bag_fees
inputs.question: For every current item in stated order, what final bag fee applies after allocating the personal-item and carry-on allowances only to qualifying items, assigning the remaining items successive checked positions, applying route, cabin and complimentary benefits, applying the correct weight allowance and overweight band, summing outside dimensions for the oversize band, and adding only the higher simultaneous overweight or oversize fee? Return zero for an item carried without charge.

skill.intent: Return the exact integer ticket price plus the final applicable fee for every current bag.

outputs.description: Exact integer ticket price plus all applicable fees for every current bag.
outputs.name: answer

fields.name: ticket_price
fields.question: What ticket price is stated for the current passenger?

fields.name: per_item_final_bag_fees
fields.question: What complete fee applies to each current item in order, using zero for an item carried without charge?

reads.question: Jointly classify and price every current item under the applicable carried-item allowances, checked-bag positions, route, cabin, complimentary benefits, weight rules, and size rules while preserving item order.
reads.source_locator: current RuleArena Airline source_text, facts, and question

origin.quote: You're allowed 1 carry-on bag and 1 personal item in all cabins.

source_obligations.statement: Allocate no more than one qualifying personal item and one qualifying carry-on before assigning checked-bag positions.

origin.quote:
1st and 2nd checked bags are complimentary for:
* AAdvantage Platinum® status
* oneworld® Sapphire members
* Confirmed Domestic First customers
* Confirmed Business customers
* Confirmed Premium Economy customers

source_obligations.statement: For each remaining item, apply its successive checked position together with the current route, cabin, and complimentary-bag benefits.

origin.quote: The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

source_obligations.statement: For each checked item that is both overweight and oversize, add only the higher excess fee to its checked-bag fee.

source_provenance.quote: The total size of your carry-on, including the handles and wheels, cannot exceed 22 x 14 x 9 inches (56 x 36 x 23 cm) and must fit in the sizer at the airport.
For First / Business, weight is 70 lbs / 32 kgs for complimentary bags and 50 lbs / 23 kgs for excess charged bags
We calculate the size limits of your bag by adding the total outside dimensions of each bag, length + width + height.
More than one fee may apply per bag that exceeds standard dimensions for both weight and size. The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.
